candidates.name: llm-chain-2
candidates.source:
NAME = "chain-2"   # two-step lookahead: value now + discounted second wave

def objective(f, state, region_mask, chosen, graph, prob):
    P0 = prob(f.a)
    P1 = prob(f.a + 1)
    D = np.where(f.eligible, P1 - P0, 0.0)      # expected activation per target with one more exposure
    own = f.eligible * (1.0 - P0)               # the seed itself
    inflow = D @ graph.adjT                     # what a node, once activated, is expected to trigger next round
    second = (D * inflow) @ graph.adjT          # second wave credited to the seeds that produced those nodes
    return D @ graph.adjT + own + 0.6 * second + 1e-3 * f.eligible

candidates.name: llm-thrifty-expose
candidates.source:
NAME = "thrifty-expose"   # only spend exposures that are likely to convert (fatigue economy)

def objective(f, state, region_mask, chosen, graph, prob):
    P0 = prob(f.a)
    P1 = prob(f.a + 1)
    D = np.where(f.eligible, P1 - P0, 0.0)
    # an exposure that leaves the node short of the gate is pure loss for laws with
    # exposure memory (unproductive exposures depress future hazard), so charge for it
    weak = np.where(f.eligible, (P1 < 0.5).astype(float), 0.0)
    waste = 0.35 * weak * (1.0 - P1)
    score = np.where(f.eligible, D, 0.0) - waste
    return score @ graph.adjT + f.eligible * (1.0 - P0) + 1e-3 * f.eligible

candidates.name: llm-gate-future
candidates.source:
NAME = "gate-future"   # complete gates, and credit what the completed nodes activate next round

def objective(f, state, region_mask, chosen, graph, prob):
    P0 = prob(f.a)
    P1 = prob(f.a + 1)
    D = np.where(f.eligible, P1 - P0, 0.0)
    comp = (f.eligible & (f.a == 1)).astype(float)   # one more exposure crosses the (soft) gate
    prog = (f.eligible & (f.a == 0)).astype(float)   # paving for the following round
    base = comp + 0.4 * prog
    first = base @ graph.adjT                        # gates this seed completes/paves
    F = D @ graph.adjT                               # spread value of a target if it activates
    future = 0.6 * ((base * F) @ graph.adjT)         # second wave triggered by this seed's completions
    return first + future + 0.3 * (D @ graph.adjT) + f.eligible * (1.0 - P0) + 1e-3 * f.eligible

candidates.name: llm-two-hop-lead
candidates.source:
NAME = "two-hop-lead"   # does what hub misses: values landing targets whose own
                        # out-reach fires next round (chains the margin)

def objective(f, state, region_mask, chosen, graph, prob):
    P0 = prob(f.a)
    P1 = prob(f.a + 1)
    # marginal activation of each target if it gets one more active in-neighbour now
    D = np.where(f.eligible, P1 - P0, 0.0)
    # a target t that activates this round becomes an active in-neighbour next round,
    # so seeding via t also picks up t's own spread margin next round
    fut = D @ graph.adjT
    C = D * (1.0 + 0.6 * fut)
    # routing the per-target contribution to seeds, plus the seed's own activation,
    # plus a small reach term so gains never tie flat (keeps greedy ties sensible)
    return C @ graph.adjT + f.eligible * D + 1e-3 * f.eligible

candidates.name: llm-stair-finish
candidates.source:
NAME = "stair-finish"   # does what gate-2 misses: rewards pushing a target all the
                        # way to certainty (a second exposure next round is valued
                        # weighted by the probability the landing actually happens)

def objective(f, state, region_mask, chosen, graph, prob):
    P0 = prob(f.a)
    P1 = prob(f.a + 1)
    P2 = prob(f.a + 2)
    D = np.where(f.eligible, P1 - P0, 0.0)          # value of one more exposure now
    D2 = np.where(f.eligible, P2 - P1, 0.0)         # value of a further exposure
    land = np.where(f.eligible, P1, 0.0)             # chance the target lands this round
    # per-target contribution: launch now, plus a discounted second-hit payoff that
    # only banks if the target actually activates in between
    C = D + 0.5 * land * D2
    return C @ graph.adjT + f.eligible * D + 1e-3 * f.eligible

candidates.name: llm-fatigue-lean
candidates.source:
NAME = "fatigue-lean"   # does what no existing operator does: since gamma=1 laws carry
                        # exposure memory, nodes with many past unproductive exposures
                        # give degraded returns; lean the margin away from them
                        # (only matters under fatigue hypotheses, harmless otherwise)

def objective(f, state, region_mask, chosen, graph, prob):
    P0 = prob(f.a)
    P1 = prob(f.a + 1)
    D = np.where(f.eligible, P1 - P0, 0.0)
    # number of past exposures that have NOT produced activation so far
    past = np.clip(f.E - f.a, 0.0, None)
    rust = 1.0 / (1.0 + 0.3 * past)                  # saturating penalty on burnt targets
    C = D * rust
    # seed's own activation is also degraded by its own exposure history
    own = f.eligible * D * rust
    return C @ graph.adjT + own + 1e-3 * f.eligible

candidates.name: llm-cascade-2
candidates.source:
NAME = "cascade-2"   # one-step spread plus next-round cascade value

def objective(f, state, region_mask, chosen, graph, prob):
    P0 = prob(f.a)
    P1 = prob(f.a + 1)
    D = np.where(f.eligible, P1 - P0, 0.0)          # marginal activation of each target
    one = D @ graph.adjT + f.eligible * (1.0 - P0)  # hub's one-round gain
    # second order: a target v activated this round becomes an active in-neighbour
    # next round and adds (D @ adjT)[v] to the following round's expected gain
    carry = D @ graph.adjT
    second = (D * carry) @ graph.adjT
    return one + second + 1e-3 * f.eligible

candidates.name: llm-synergy-2
candidates.source:
NAME = "synergy-2"   # weight targets by their pairwise-synergy second marginal

def objective(f, state, region_mask, chosen, graph, prob):
    P0 = prob(f.a)
    P1 = prob(f.a + 1)
    P2 = prob(f.a + 2)
    D1 = P1 - P0                     # first marginal (what hub uses)
    D2 = P2 - 2.0 * P1 + P0          # second marginal: big where synergy bites
    w = np.clip(1.0 + 3.0 * D2, 0.1, 4.0)   # boost near-gate, synergy-rich targets
    X = np.where(f.eligible, D1 * w, 0.0)
    own = f.eligible * (1.0 - P0) * w
    return X @ graph.adjT + own + 1e-3 * f.eligible

candidates.name: llm-fresh-cascade
candidates.source:
NAME = "fresh-cascade"   # cascade value discounted by neighbourhood fatigue

def objective(f, state, region_mask, chosen, graph, prob):
    P0 = prob(f.a)
    P1 = prob(f.a + 1)
    D = np.where(f.eligible, P1 - P0, 0.0)
    past = np.maximum(f.E - f.a, 0.0)
    fresh = 1.0 / (1.0 + past)   # targets with little accumulated exposure keep
                                 # their future hazard (exp(-c*past)) high, so
                                 # activating them pays off over several rounds
    DF = D * fresh
    one = DF @ graph.adjT + f.eligible * (1.0 - P0)
    second = (DF * (DF @ graph.adjT)) @ graph.adjT
    # don't burn exposure on targets that will fire this round anyway
    sat = np.clip(1.0 - P1, 0.0, 1.0)
    return one + second * sat + 1e-3 * f.eligible

candidates.name: llm-fresh-synergy
candidates.source:
NAME = "fresh-synergy"

def objective(f, state, region_mask, chosen, graph, prob):
    # Hub-style one-round value, but every target's marginal is discounted by how
    # much exposure (fatigue) it already carries. H0's hazard decays as
    # exp(-c * (E - a)), so pushing an already-saturated target wastes the seed;
    # fresh targets convert the same +1 in-neighbour into far more probability.
    # This trades raw spread (hub) for spread that actually lands while it can.
    P0, P1 = prob(f.a), prob(f.a + 1)
    D = np.where(f.eligible, P1 - P0, 0.0)                 # marginal per target
    past = np.maximum(f.E - f.a, 0.0)                      # excess exposure
    fresh = np.exp(-past)                                  # fatigue discount, law-agnostic
    spread = (D * fresh) @ graph.adjT
    self_gain = f.eligible * (1.0 - P0) * fresh
    # small non-zero reach term so ties break towards high-cascade candidates
    reach = 1e-3 * (D @ graph.adjT)
    return spread + self_gain + reach

candidates.name: llm-pair-3
candidates.source:
NAME = "pair-3"

def objective(f, state, region_mask, chosen, graph, prob):
    # H0's synergy term s*a*(a-1)/2 makes the jump from 2 to 3 active in-neighbours
    # disproportionately valuable (3 sources form 3 correlated pairs). Hub spreads
    # its weight over all first-order marginals and misses that structure;
    # gate-3 hard-codes the pattern but with flat weights, so greedy ties collapse
    # onto low ids. Here the bonus scales with the number of new pairs the seed
    # creates at the target, and a live prob-based reach term breaks ties by real
    # cascade value.
    P0, P1 = prob(f.a), prob(f.a + 1)
    D = np.where(f.eligible, P1 - P0, 0.0)
    # pairs gained by +1 active in-neighbour: (a+1 choose 2) - (a choose 2) = a
    new_pairs = np.where(f.eligible, f.a, 0.0)
    comp = f.eligible & (f.a >= 2)                         # targets entering the synergy regime
    prog = f.eligible & (f.a < 2)
    pair_score = (3.0 * comp * new_pairs + 0.2 * prog).astype(float)
    reach = 0.3 * (D @ graph.adjT) + 1e-3 * f.eligible     # non-zero tie-breaker
    return pair_score @ graph.adjT + reach + f.eligible * (1.0 - P0)

candidates.name: llm-two-hop
candidates.source:
NAME = "two-hop"

def objective(f, state, region_mask, chosen, graph, prob):
    # Hub only counts one round of spread. Under H0 an activated target becomes an
    # active in-neighbour next round and its own out-neighbours may already sit at
    # a=1, so the pairwise synergy means a second source triggers a big jump.
    # Score candidates by immediate spread plus a discounted second-wave term:
    # (marginal * activation prob) propagated through adjT twice, with fatigue
    # discounting on the second wave since those nodes carry prior exposure.
    P0, P1 = prob(f.a), prob(f.a + 1)
    D = np.where(f.eligible, P1 - P0, 0.0)
    wave1 = D @ graph.adjT
    past = np.maximum(f.E - f.a, 0.0)
    fresh = np.exp(-past)
    wave2 = ((D * P1 * fresh) @ graph.adjT) @ graph.adjT
    self_gain = f.eligible * (1.0 - P0)
    # keep a non-zero reach term to break ties towards genuine hubs
    return wave1 + 0.4 * wave2 + self_gain + 1e-3 * (D @ graph.adjT)

candidates.name: llm-chain-2
candidates.source:
NAME = "chain-2"   # hub + expected second-hop push

def objective(f, state, region_mask, chosen, graph, prob):
    p0 = prob(f.a)
    p1 = prob(f.a + 1)
    D = np.where(f.eligible, p1 - p0, 0.0)      # marginal activation of each target
    one = D @ graph.adjT + f.eligible * (1.0 - p0)
    # if an out-neighbour v fires this round (prob D[v]), its own out-neighbours w
    # get pushed next round: w's gain is D[w] per firing v, summed over v.
    two = (D @ graph.adjT) * D
    # degree tie-break so round 0 (where D == 0) seeds hubs, not the lowest ids
    outdeg = np.asarray(graph.adj.sum(axis=1)).ravel()
    return one + two + 1e-3 * f.eligible + 2e-3 * f.eligible * outdeg

candidates.name: llm-ladder-2
candidates.source:
NAME = "ladder-2"   # hub + damped second-hit ladder using prob(f.a + 2)

def objective(f, state, region_mask, chosen, graph, prob):
    p0 = prob(f.a)
    p1 = prob(f.a + 1)
    p2 = prob(f.a + 2)
    D1 = np.where(f.eligible, p1 - p0, 0.0)
    D2 = np.where(f.eligible, p2 - p1, 0.0)     # marginal of a *second* increment
    spread = D1 @ graph.adjT + f.eligible * (1.0 - p0)
    # v fires now with prob spread-via-D1[v]; its push on w is worth D2[w], not D1[w],
    # because w will already carry one active in-neighbour from this round.
    follow = D2 * (D1 @ graph.adjT)
    outdeg = np.asarray(graph.adj.sum(axis=1)).ravel()
    return spread + 0.7 * follow + 1e-3 * f.eligible + 2e-3 * f.eligible * outdeg

candidates.name: llm-first-hit-tilt
candidates.source:
NAME = "first-hit-tilt"   # hub tilted towards first exposures of fresh targets

def objective(f, state, region_mask, chosen, graph, prob):
    p0 = prob(f.a)
    p1 = prob(f.a + 1)
    D = np.where(f.eligible, p1 - p0, 0.0)
    # the 0 -> 1 jump is the largest marginal step under all three laws
    # (H0: dose ~ a^0.15 so repeat hits add ~2% while the first hit pays the full
    #  base hazard; H2: dose 1-(1-h)^a; H1 similar with saturation in a)
    fresh = np.where(f.eligible & (f.a == 0), D, 0.0)
    outdeg = np.asarray(graph.adj.sum(axis=1)).ravel()
    return D @ graph.adjT + f.eligible * (1.0 - p0) \
        + 0.5 * (fresh @ graph.adjT) \
        + 1e-2 * f.eligible * outdeg

candidates.name: llm-direct-marg
candidates.source:
NAME = "direct-marg"

def objective(f, state, region_mask, chosen, graph, prob):
    # Exact one-round marginal: candidate u is immediately an active in-neighbour,
    # so every out-neighbour v of u gets f.a_v + 1 (f.a includes the hypothetical pick).
    # Credit BOTH the direct activation reward of v (missed by hub, which only
    # propagates D onward) and the onward spread, so greedy sees the true per-candidate gain.
    P0 = prob(f.a)
    P1 = prob(f.a + 1)
    e = f.eligible.astype(float)
    D = e * (P1 - P0)                       # marginal activation of each target v
    onehop = (graph.adj @ D.T).T            # sum over v in out(u) of D_v  (direct reward)
    spread = D @ graph.adjT                 # v firing pushes its own marginals onward
    own = e * (1.0 - P0)                    # the seed's own activation
    reach = e * (graph.adj @ P1.T).T        # non-zero reach term for sane tie-breaks
    return onehop + 0.7 * spread + own + 1e-3 * reach

candidates.name: llm-horizon-2
candidates.source:
NAME = "horizon-2"

def objective(f, state, region_mask, chosen, graph, prob):
    # Two-round prospective value of a pick. Nodes v that fire THIS round (prob P1)
    # become active in-neighbours next round; their out-neighbours w then sit at
    # a_w + (expected new active in-nbrs). This values a seed by the activations it
    # causes now plus the marginal cascade those activations open next round --
    # the part hub's static one-round D @ adjT never captures.
    P0 = prob(f.a)
    P1 = prob(f.a + 1)
    e = f.eligible.astype(float)
    D = e * (P1 - P0)                        # marginal if v gains one in-neighbour now
    Da = e * P1                              # expected newly active this round
    n = Da @ graph.adjT                      # expected extra active in-nbrs next round
    Dnext = e * (prob(f.a + n) - P0)         # next-round marginals under that shift
    S = Dnext @ graph.adjT                   # next-round onward exposure per node
    onehop = (graph.adj @ D.T).T             # direct reward of the pick
    twohop = (graph.adj @ (Da * S).T).T      # cascade opened by nodes it flips now
    own = e * (1.0 - P0)
    reach = e * (graph.adj @ P1.T).T
    return onehop + 0.7 * twohop + own + 1e-3 * reach

candidates.name: llm-decay-harvest
candidates.source:
NAME = "decay-harvest"

def objective(f, state, region_mask, chosen, graph, prob):
    # Fatigue-aware scheduling. Every round a node stays exposed-but-unfired its
    # hazard decays geometrically (prob falls with E - a). So a pick that FIRES
    # already-committed nodes (f.a > 0) this round saves value that waiting destroys,
    # while leaving fresh nodes unexposed costs almost nothing. Score candidates by
    # committed-node harvest first, onward spread second, with an explicit bonus for
    # finishing off deeply fatigued targets before they decay further.
    P0 = prob(f.a)
    P1 = prob(f.a + 1)
    e = f.eligible.astype(float)
    D = e * (P1 - P0)
    w = np.where(f.a > 0, 1.0, 0.35)         # committed nodes: harvest now
    Dh = e * D * w
    onehop = (graph.adj @ Dh.T).T            # weighted direct activation reward
    spread = 0.4 * (D @ graph.adjT)          # onward potential (down-weighted)
    fatigued = e * (f.E - f.a >= 1.0) * P1 * (1.0 - P0 / np.maximum(P1, 1e-9))
    urgency = (graph.adj @ fatigued.T).T     # prefer picks that close fatigued gates
    own = e * (1.0 - P0)
    reach = e * (graph.adj @ P1.T).T
    return onehop + spread + 0.3 * urgency + own + 1e-3 * reach
